A.explanation: Changing the supply voltage scales the p.d. across the upper fixed resistor plus LDR and across the uniform wire by the same factor, so the imbalance remains.

B.explanation: Increasing the supply voltage increases currents in both parallel branches proportionally and does not restore the lost equality of the two potentials at the ammeter.

C.explanation: Covering the LDR increases its resistance so the junction potential moves toward the left-hand supply terminal, and moving the sliding contact left moves the wire potential the same way to restore balance.

D.explanation: Moving the sliding contact to the right moves the wire potential toward the right-hand supply terminal, opposite to the shift of the upper junction potential when LDR resistance rises.

hints: Notice the zero ammeter reading means the potential at the junction of the fixed resistor and LDR equals the potential at the sliding contact on the uniform wire.
Recall that covering the LDR increases its resistance, so for the series pair of fixed resistor and LDR a larger share of the supply p.d. appears across the LDR.

Think about which end of the uniform wire is at the same potential as the left side of the circuit, and which way the contact must slide to make the wire potential follow the shifted junction potential.
walkthrough: Zero current in the ammeter is a null balance: $V_{junction} = V_{contact}$, where $V_{junction}$ is between the fixed resistor on the left and the LDR on the right, and $V_{contact}$ is on the uniform wire.
Covering the LDR increases its resistance $R_{LDR}$. The upper current $I = V_{supply}/(R + R_{LDR})$ decreases.
The p.d. across the left fixed resistor is $IR$, so it decreases. Hence $V_{junction}$ moves closer to the potential of the left-hand supply terminal.

On the uniform wire the potential varies steadily from the left terminal value to the right terminal value, so moving the sliding contact to the left moves $V_{contact}$ toward the left-hand terminal value.
That leftward move compensates for the shift in $V_{junction}$ and can make $V_{junction} = V_{contact}$ again with no current in the ammeter. This is option C.
